title: Enhancing Credit Scoring with Multimodal Deep Learning: A Hybrid Neural Network Approach Using Structured and Unstructured Financial Data
authors: Hossain, M. R.; Pabel, M. A. H.; Haque, M. S. U.; Khan, M. S.; Obaid, M. O.; Akter, S.; Ahmed, M.
venue: International Interdisciplinary Business Economics Advancement Journal
tldr: A hybrid deep neural network combining structured financial data and unstructured text achieves 87% accuracy and 0.91 AUC-ROC in credit scoring, outperforming logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional credit scoring models rely on structured data and fail to evaluate borrowers with limited credit histories or non-traditional financial behaviors. Unstructured data sources such as customer service interactions, financial news, and social media sentiment contain behavioral signals not captured by conventional metrics. Integrating these multimodal data sources into a unified model remains an open challenge.
approach: Collected a multimodal dataset of over 100,000 loan profiles combining Lending Club, Give Me Some Credit, customer service logs, financial news, and Twitter sentiment data.
Preprocessed structured data with mean/mode imputation and Min-Max scaling, and unstructured text with cleaning, stopword removal, lemmatization, and spell correction.
Used pre-trained GloVe embeddings to convert text into dense vector representations, with experiments on BERT contextual embeddings.
Developed a hybrid DNN with a feedforward branch for structured data and a Bi-LSTM branch for unstructured text, merged through fully connected layers.
Applied binary cross-entropy loss and Adam optimizer with learning rate 0.001, trained for 20 epochs with early stopping.
Validated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 80/20 train-test splits and grid search for hyperparameter tuning.
Benchmarked against logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, text-only Bi-LSTM, and structured-only DNN models.
Used SHAP values to interpret feature importance from both numerical and semantic inputs.
findings: num: Hybrid DNN achieved 87% accuracy and 0.91 AUC-ROC, outperforming all baseline models.
num: Logistic regression achieved only 76% accuracy and 0.78 AUC-ROC, the lowest among all tested models.
num: XGBoost reached 85% accuracy and 0.89 AUC-ROC, the strongest structured-data-only performer.
num: Bi-LSTM on text alone achieved 83% accuracy, 84% recall, and 0.88 AUC-ROC, validating text-based predictive signals.
num: Structured-only DNN achieved 84% accuracy and 0.89 AUC-ROC, slightly above Bi-LSTM but below the hybrid.
num: Hybrid model precision was 82%, recall 85%, and F1-score 83.5%, demonstrating balanced classification.
SHAP analysis showed credit utilization and sentiment-laden text were key predictive features for loan default.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Dataset details across structured and unstructured sources → multimodal dataset spans 100K+ records from five sources.
Table 2: Model performance comparison across six algorithms → hybrid DNN dominates all metrics.
Chart 1: Comparative bar chart of five metrics across all models → visual confirmation of hybrid model superiority.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a hybrid deep learning architecture that fuses structured financial data with unstructured textual data for credit scoring. It provides empirical evidence that multimodal approaches outperform single-modality and traditional machine learning methods. The study establishes benchmarks across six model configurations, offering a comparative reference for future credit risk modeling research. It also demonstrates the value of textual behavioral signals, such as customer service sentiment, as predictive features in financial risk assessment.
directly_justifies: Hybrid DNN combining structured and unstructured data achieves 87% accuracy and 0.91 AUC-ROC in credit scoring.
Bi-LSTM on text alone achieves 83% accuracy, validating textual behavioral signals as predictive for credit risk.
SHAP analysis identifies credit utilization and sentiment-laden text as key predictive features.
XGBoost with structured data only reaches 85% accuracy, demonstrating ceiling without unstructured inputs.
limits: Dataset specifics beyond size are not fully disclosed, limiting reproducibility.
The study does not address real-time deployment or latency constraints in production environments.
Model interpretability for regulatory compliance is acknowledged but not deeply evaluated.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as high relevance due to the core contribution of a deep learning credit risk model. Domain 12 (Evaluation) was flagged as high relevance because the paper provides extensive comparative evaluation across six algorithms and five metrics. Domain 14 (ML Deployment) was assigned medium relevance as the paper discusses deployment implications but without implementation specifics. Domain 4 (Existing Systems Landscape) received low relevance for its literature review of existing credit scoring approaches. Domain 10 (Data Privacy) received low relevance as GDPR/HIPAA compliance is mentioned but not a core focus. Borderline cases included Domain 3 (Expense Categorization) and Domain 11 (Engagement), both rejected as the paper focuses on credit risk prediction rather than expense management or user engagement. The paper's topical coverage centers on predictive modeling and algorithmic evaluation for financial risk assessment.

limitations: Data sources and preprocessing details are not fully reproducible from the description provided.
Real-time deployment feasibility and computational cost are not evaluated.
Regulatory compliance and model interpretability for financial audits are acknowledged as challenges but not addressed in depth.
The study uses historical data and does not validate the model on prospective or live lending data.
